controls.reason: The assessment status is a closed four-value field, so every control row can be checked against the allowed enumeration.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every control in the assessment registry has exactly one status equal to Pass, Fail, Blocked, or Not Applicable.

controls.reason: A rationale field and review record are objective, but deciding that the rationale is substantively tied to system context requires accountable interpretation.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every Not Applicable row contains nonempty context identifiers, rationale text, reviewer identity, and review timestamp.

controls.reason: A bounded applicable-control registry, owner field, evidence validity policy, and rerun recipe make ownership, currency, and reproducibility decidable.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every applicable control has exactly one accountable owner and evidence within its versioned validity period.
Every evidence reproduction recipe completes with the same declared result against the bound assessment inputs.

controls.reason: All named evidence bindings are exact identifiers or timestamps whose presence and referential integrity can be validated mechanically.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every evidence record identifies product, source revision, artifact digest, configuration version, environment, data-state identifier, and assessment date.

controls.reason: Change and reassessment timestamps are observable, but materiality, affected-control scope, and proportionate reassessment depth require contextual risk judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Each change declared material links to invalidated evidence identifiers and a later reassessment record.

controls.reason: A structured exception schema and expiry enforcement make bounded duration, ownership, monitoring, documentation, and automatic expiration objectively testable.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every exception has risk owner, start and end times, monitoring references, and documented scope.
Expired exceptions are automatically inactive and cannot authorize a current Pass or release decision.

controls.reason: Supplier attribution is a structured property, so the registry can require the control to remain assessed and retain an internal accountable owner.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every supplier-operated control remains in the assessment registry and has one internal accountable owner even when implementing responsibility is shared.

controls.reason: Gate configuration is observable, but classifying a failure as serious depends on impact and release context not fixed by this statement.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every failure marked serious in the approved severity register independently blocks release regardless of aggregate score.

controls.reason: Boundary records can be required, but deciding whether product, system, organization, release, and lifecycle boundaries are complete and meaningful is contextual.

deterministic_clauses.statement: The assessment record contains explicit product, service, system, organization, release, and lifecycle boundary fields.

controls.reason: Known assets can be listed, but proving that every component, interface, supplier, location, and operational process has been discovered is an unbounded completeness claim.

deterministic_clauses.statement: The approved scope manifest contains entries for each required asset and actor category.

controls.reason: A module trigger matrix is mechanically evaluable once facts are declared, but jurisdiction, contractual, and risk applicability require specialist or accountable judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every declared capability, user, data, jurisdiction, contract, and risk trigger maps to an enabled or explicitly inapplicable conditional module.

controls.reason: The corpus and assessment registry are finite, so control identifiers can be compared exactly and omissions detected.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every control identifier in the bound corpus version appears exactly once in the assessment registry with a status.

controls.reason: The permitted assessment statuses form an exact enumeration with no subjective threshold or external scope.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every assessment status is exactly Pass, Fail, Blocked, or Not Applicable.

controls.reason: A fixed approval rule can treat Blocked as failure unless the same record contains an authenticated authorized override.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Final approval fails for every Blocked control unless that control links to an authenticated authorized decision explicitly overriding the default.

controls.reason: Presence of a control-specific rationale is objective, but whether it is specific enough to justify inapplicability requires contextual review.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every Not Applicable control has a nonempty rationale linked to that control and the assessed system context.

controls.reason: Structured prohibited reason codes can be rejected mechanically, but detecting those motives when hidden in free-form rationale requires contextual interpretation.

deterministic_clauses.statement: A Not Applicable result is rejected when its only declared rationale codes are inconvenience, cost, external ownership, tool limitation, or missing implementation.

controls.reason: Applicable controls and exceptions are finite registries, so exact-one accountable-owner cardinality is mechanically decidable.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every applicable control and every exception has exactly one active accountable-owner identifier.

controls.reason: Reviewer identity and separation can be queried, but qualification, materiality, and sufficient independence require accountable governance judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Each control declared material records reviewer identity, reviewer role, approval, and organizational relationship to the implementer.

controls.reason: The required evidence context consists of exact version and environment bindings whose presence and referential integrity are decidable.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Each evidence item is bound to source revision, artifact digest, configuration, schema, flags, environment, dependency versions, and data-state identifier.

controls.reason: Release and environment mismatches are objective, but whether an equivalence demonstration is technically sufficient requires contextual validation.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Evidence from a different release or environment is rejected unless it links to a versioned equivalence record.

controls.reason: Choosing validity periods from change rate, threat evolution, supplier change, and control volatility is a risk-calibration decision with no fixed formula here.
Change-to-evidence timestamps can be compared, but deciding whether a change is material and can affect a conclusion requires contextual impact analysis.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Evidence linked to a change declared material is marked invalid no later than that change's effective timestamp.

controls.reason: The sampling requirement names a finite set of required fields that can be checked in each sampling record.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every sampled assessment records population, method, coverage, confidence, limitations, and risk rationale.

controls.reason: Preferring one evidence item over another requires judging directness, relevance, and context; the statement supplies no mechanical ordering rule.
Given declared primary-control absence conditions and compensating-control expectations, bounded tests can directly prove operation under those conditions.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every compensating control has a current successful test executed under each declared condition in which the primary control is absent.

controls.reason: Inherent and residual risk are distinct structured record fields whose post-control ordering and presence can be validated exactly.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every assessed risk records residual risk after linked controls as well as inherent risk before those controls.

controls.reason: A scoring and release-gate policy is bounded code or configuration that can be inspected for forbidden offsetting of critical failures.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Any critical failure forces the configured aggregate decision to fail regardless of scores from unrelated controls.

controls.reason: Severity definitions and their publication time can be compared with assessment-result timestamps to prove they were fixed in advance.

deterministic_clauses.statement: The versioned severity policy defines blocking and nonblocking levels and predates every assessment result evaluated under it.

controls.reason: Conflict records and escalation routes are observable, but recognizing a quality-attribute conflict and selecting a qualified multidisciplinary owner require human judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every declared cross-attribute conflict links to an authorized decision owner and escalation record.

controls.reason: Storage controls can be queried, but whether durability, immutability, and access restrictions are proportionate to risk requires contextual judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Evidence repositories expose authenticated retention, access-control, search-index, and immutable or tamper-evident storage settings.

controls.reason: Bounded secret and sensitive-data detectors can flag known patterns, but proving absence of all personal, vulnerability, or customer information is unbounded.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Assessment evidence has results from the approved secret, personal-data, and sensitive-content detectors before storage or publication.

controls.reason: Reviewing inherited provider controls and deciding which customer responsibilities remain requires accountable interpretation of shared-responsibility contracts.
Trigger events and reassessment records can be matched, but material findings and significant scale changes require contextual classification.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every recorded incident, escaped defect, supplier or jurisdiction change, and change marked major or significant links to a later reassessment.

controls.reason: Immutable version identifiers and append-only storage can prove that historical assessments remain linked to historical releases and were not overwritten.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every historical release references an immutable historical assessment version, and no later assessment mutation replaces that version.

controls.reason: Corpus diffs can detect deleted universal controls, but deciding which additional domain, organization, product, and jurisdiction controls are necessary requires specialist context.

deterministic_clauses.statement: The derived corpus contains every universal control identifier from its declared baseline or an explicit versioned retirement record.

controls.reason: Control identifier and full control text are exact required evidence-record fields with a direct corpus comparison.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every evidence record contains the control identifier and text exactly matching the bound corpus revision.

controls.reason: Assessment status is a required structured field whose presence and allowed value can be checked exactly.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every minimum evidence record contains one allowed assessment status.

controls.reason: Applicability rationale is an explicit required evidence-record field whose nonempty presence can be checked.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every minimum evidence record contains a nonempty applicability-rationale field.

controls.reason: Accountable owner is an exact required identity field whose presence and referential validity are mechanically decidable.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every minimum evidence record contains one resolvable accountable-owner identifier.

controls.reason: Implementing owner or team is an exact required identity field whose presence can be validated against the organization directory.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every minimum evidence record contains a resolvable implementing-owner or team identifier.

controls.reason: Reviewer identity and approval are explicit record fields whose signatures and presence can be validated.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every minimum evidence record contains a reviewer identifier and authenticated approval.

controls.reason: Evidence location and access classification are exact required fields with resolvable references and enumerated values.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every minimum evidence record contains a resolvable evidence location and an allowed access-classification value.

controls.reason: Evidence date and expiry are exact timestamps whose presence and ordering can be checked mechanically.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every minimum evidence record contains an evidence date and a later expiry timestamp.

controls.reason: The named system and version context values are exact required fields whose bindings can be validated.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every minimum evidence record identifies system, component, environment, source revision, artifact digest, configuration, schema, flags, and dependency context.

controls.reason: The test metadata categories are explicit required record fields and can be checked for presence and version bindings.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every minimum evidence record contains method, data, tools, tool versions, assumptions, and limitations.

controls.reason: Observed result and threshold are exact required fields that can be checked for presence and compatible typed values.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every minimum evidence record contains an observed result and the threshold used to evaluate it.

controls.reason: The linked issue categories are resolvable reference fields whose presence or explicit empty state can be validated.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every minimum evidence record contains resolvable defect, risk, exception, incident, or corrective-action links, or an explicit none value.

controls.reason: Reassessment trigger is an explicit required field that can be checked against the allowed trigger schema.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every minimum evidence record contains a versioned reassessment-trigger definition.

controls.reason: An exception can be matched to one control and required to contain an explicit incomplete-remediation explanation.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every exception identifies exactly one unmet control and contains a nonempty reason remediation is incomplete.

controls.reason: Presence of affected-scope descriptions is objective, but proving that all affected users, systems, data, operations, and outcomes were found is unbounded.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every exception record contains affected users, systems, data, operations, and business-outcome fields.

controls.reason: Likelihood, impact, exploitability, reach, detectability, recoverability, and duration are risk judgments whose scales and evidence rules are not defined here.
Existing and proposed compensating controls are two explicit exception-record collections whose presence and identifiers are decidable.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every exception documents its existing and proposed compensating controls with resolvable control identifiers.

controls.reason: Versioned compensating-control expectations and current authenticated results can mechanically demonstrate operation for the accepted-risk conditions.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every compensating control linked to an exception has current successful execution evidence under the exception's declared conditions.

controls.reason: Risk-specific monitor definitions and alert thresholds are exact structured values that can be required in each exception.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every accepted-risk record defines monitoring queries, alert thresholds, comparison operators, windows, and notification routes.

controls.reason: Owner identity and role scope are observable, but whether that person is authorized over the consequences requires accountable governance judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every accepted risk identifies one active risk owner and the recorded authority scope attached to that role.

controls.reason: Owner, funding, target date, and automatic-expiry configuration are exact exception fields and state transitions.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every exception has a remediation owner, funded-plan reference, target date, and automatic expiry timestamp.

controls.reason: Immediate revocation conditions are a required structured set whose presence and evaluable predicates can be checked.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every exception defines at least one machine-readable immediate-revocation condition.

controls.reason: Expiry and renewal histories can prove that exceptions deactivate automatically and never renew without a new authorized decision.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every exception becomes inactive at its expiry timestamp unless a separate newly approved exception exists.
Exception history contains no silent extension or reuse as an unbounded permanent architecture authorization.

controls.reason: Cumulative risk interaction and acceptability across multiple exceptions require accountable portfolio judgment rather than independent field validation.
Delivery to declared recipients is objective, but deciding which functions and customers are appropriate recipients requires context and sometimes legal judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Each exception has authenticated communication evidence for every recipient declared required in its communication plan.

controls.reason: Remediation state and review records are observable, but determining remediation sufficiency and reviewer independence requires accountable judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: A closed exception links to completed remediation evidence and a later verification record from a different recorded reviewer.

controls.reason: Selecting and ranking quality attributes across users, law, threats, failure cost, and strategy is an accountable multidisciplinary prioritization decision.
Scenario and threshold fields are objective, but identifying every material quality attribute requires contextual risk and stakeholder judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every quality attribute marked material has a measurable scenario and numeric or enumerated acceptance threshold.

controls.reason: Recognizing trade-offs and proving that optimization did not silently harm another quality attribute requires cross-attribute causal and value judgment.
Evidence types can be labeled and linked, but deciding whether real-world quality-in-use evidence is representative and sufficient requires contextual judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Each material quality objective links to both product-quality evidence and a quality-in-use evidence record.

controls.reason: Distribution outputs are computable, but selecting complete edge populations and degraded conditions requires context-specific risk judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Each declared quality measure reports a distribution and results for every versioned edge-population and degraded-condition cohort.

controls.reason: Quality budgets, regression limits, and publication timestamps can be compared with implementation and launch timestamps.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every material quality objective has a versioned budget and regression limit effective before implementation and launch.

controls.reason: Quality objectives and recorded conflicts are finite registries, allowing exact-one ownership checks.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every quality objective and every registered cross-attribute conflict has exactly one accountable owner.

controls.reason: A versioned traceability graph can require resolvable links from each objective to all named implementation and operational artifact classes.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every quality objective links to architecture tactics, code, tests, monitoring, and operational-decision records.

controls.reason: Event and review dates can be matched, but materiality and relevance of incidents, scale, populations, or regulation changes require contextual or specialist judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every qualifying trigger event in the approved change register links to a later quality-objective review.

controls.reason: A scanner cannot prove that no overall-quality claim anywhere relies on a single score, certification, test level, or lack of reported defects.
Declared requirements and test results can be traced, but completeness for intended tasks and contexts depends on product and user judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every required function in the approved requirements inventory has current successful evidence for its declared tasks and contexts.

controls.reason: Correctness of all results, state transitions, permissions, and side effects across arbitrary behavior cannot be proven from bounded tests or static analysis.
Whether behavior is unnecessary or inappropriate and whether users can complete intended tasks require product and usability judgment in context.
Versioned scenarios and their test results are objective, but completeness of exceptional, degraded, recovery, cancellation, and prohibited behavior is contextual.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every scenario in the approved exceptional-behavior inventory is defined and has a current verification result.

controls.reason: Defined performance objectives and specified test conditions provide fixed metrics, thresholds, and bounded executions for exact comparison.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every applicable latency, throughput, responsiveness, and completion-time objective defines a metric, condition, and threshold.
Current authenticated measurements under each specified condition satisfy every defined threshold.

controls.reason: Whether compute, memory, storage, network, energy, and provider use are proportionate to outcomes is a value and cost judgment without fixed ratios.
Versioned capacity limits and expected overload responses provide finite boundary and overload tests with exact outcomes.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every declared capacity boundary and safe-overload behavior has a current successful bounded test result.

controls.reason: Representative devices, networks, volumes, tenants, and failures and the meaning of acceptable performance are not fixed by this control.
Safe coexistence in shared environments depends on workload interference, isolation objectives, user impact, and risk tolerance not specified here.
A complete interface contract can define exact syntax, semantics, precision, identity, ordering, privacy, and authorization invariants for bounded exchange tests.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every supported information exchange has a versioned contract for syntax, semantics, precision, identity, ordering, privacy, and authorization.
Bounded contract tests for every supported exchange satisfy all declared invariants.

controls.reason: A declared support matrix and promised behavior contracts create a finite cross-product of versions, formats, clients, protocols, and environments to test.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every cell in the promised support matrix has a current successful interoperability test result.

controls.reason: Negotiation, migration, deprecation, and retirement artifacts are observable, but whether their control is sufficient for each incompatible change requires contextual judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every change declared incompatible links to versioned negotiation, migration, deprecation, and retirement records.

controls.reason: Recognizing product appropriateness is a user outcome that requires a representative study, but no population, task, measure, or threshold is defined.
Effective learning and operation with reasonable effort require user research, while representative users, effort measures, and thresholds are undefined.
Whether the product adequately prevents, identifies, explains, and supports recovery from user error requires task-based evaluation with undefined populations and thresholds.
Inclusion across abilities, language, literacy, devices, inputs, and contexts requires accessibility, localization, and user-research expertise plus applicability judgment.
System understandability from help, feedback, status, and self-description is a user outcome without a defined study population, task set, measure, or threshold.
Manipulation and preservation of user autonomy require ethical, product, and sometimes legal judgment that bounded interface scans cannot settle.
Required functions, observed faults, and test results can be recorded, but unacceptable fault levels and sufficient specified conditions require contextual reliability objectives.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every declared required function has fault measurements from each condition in the approved reliability test plan.

controls.reason: User-centric availability objectives supply exact indicators, windows, and thresholds that authenticated service telemetry can evaluate.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Authenticated availability measurements meet every versioned user-centric objective for its declared window.

controls.reason: Determining complete fault boundaries, cascade causality, and whether propagation was unnecessary requires architecture and incident judgment beyond finite tests.
Approved recovery time, recovery point, integrity, and continuity objectives give exact acceptance limits for bounded recovery exercises.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every declared recovery scenario has a current exercise result meeting its approved time, point, integrity, and continuity thresholds.

controls.reason: Reliability results are objective, but complete and representative deployment, dependency, overload, maintenance, and disaster scenarios require contextual risk selection.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every scenario in the approved cross-condition reliability matrix has current measurements satisfying its declared objectives.

controls.reason: Proving that no unauthorized party can access any information or operation is an unbounded security claim; bounded access tests only cover known paths.
Complete integrity of data, code, configuration, identities, and actions across all changes and attacks cannot be proven by a finite scan or test set.
Audit-event coverage is measurable for declared actions, but which actions are material and what audit detail is appropriate require security and governance judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every action marked material in the approved action inventory emits an attributable audit record with actor, target, action, result, and time.

controls.reason: Authentication tests and assurance metadata are objective, but the required assurance level for each identity, service, device, artifact, and message is context-dependent.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every item in the approved authentication inventory has current evidence meeting its declared assurance level.

controls.reason: Resistance to all attack, abuse, bypass, compromise, and unauthorized recovery paths is adversarial and open-ended, so bounded testing cannot prove the full claim.
Security effectiveness across the complete development, supply-chain, deployment, operation, and retirement lifecycle is an open-ended assurance claim requiring specialist review.
Modularity enough to localize understanding, change, testing, and failure depends on architecture, team, and change patterns with no fixed structural metric.
Usefulness, unsafe coupling, and semantic mismatch in reuse are design judgments that depend on the asset and consumer context.
Whether defects, state, dependencies, and performance can be analyzed efficiently depends on tasks, tools, expertise, and an undefined efficiency threshold.
Safe implementation, review, verification, deployment, and reversal depend on change-specific risks and adequacy of the process, not merely artifact presence.
Whether ownership, documents, tests, tools, and environments sufficiently support unknown future maintainers requires human assessment and an undefined support threshold.
Required adaptation and uncontrolled redesign depend on future environments, users, workloads, and architecture strategy not bounded by this rule.
Required demand, preserved quality, and safe overload behavior require workload forecasts and quality thresholds not supplied by this statement.
Reliable and supportable installation, deployment, configuration, upgrade, and migration require scenario, support, and failure thresholds that are not defined.
Whether replacement is required and practically possible depends on continuity objectives, contracts, architecture, cost, and strategy.
Controllable inputs and observable-output hooks can be inventoried, but whether isolation and reproducibility make the product sufficiently testable is contextual.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every declared test interface documents controllable inputs, observable outputs, isolation mechanism, and reproduction procedure.

controls.reason: Identifying unacceptable hazardous states and deciding whether operational constraints prevent them requires safety engineering and accountable hazard acceptance.
Foreseeability and completeness of hazards and affected people, property, business, software, and environment require qualified hazard analysis.
When fail-safe behavior is required and whether it adequately limits harm are safety decisions tied to hazards and assumptions.
Timeliness, perceptibility, and actionability of warnings depend on hazards and users and require empirical or specialist evaluation without defined thresholds.
Proving integrations do not invalidate any safety control requires complete hazard and interface analysis by qualified safety specialists.
Residual safety risk review and acceptance are explicitly independent human and authorized-leadership decisions that automation must not substitute.
Goal accuracy and completeness for representative users require an empirical study, but population, goals, measures, and acceptance thresholds are unspecified.
Acceptable time, effort, cognitive load, cost, and resource use are user-study outcomes with no defined population, tasks, or thresholds.
Trust, comfort, usefulness, satisfaction, and freedom from manipulation require user research and ethical judgment, with no fixed measurement contract.
Acceptable economic, health, safety, privacy, security, social, and environmental risk requires multidisciplinary and often legal or safety authority.
The full range of intended and foreseeable contexts is not bounded, and acceptable quality across all of it requires contextual and empirical judgment.
Support during interruption, disability, stress, poor connectivity, device limits, and emergencies must be evaluated with users and scenarios not defined here.
Outcome telemetry and linked revisions are observable, but choosing meaningful real-world outcomes and deciding how evidence should revise assumptions require product judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Each declared real-world outcome has current monitoring and links from material observations to a quality-assumption review or revision record.

controls.reason: The crosswalk's intended status can be enforced through an explicit baseline disclaimer and prohibition on universal applicability claims.

deterministic_clauses.statement: The crosswalk documentation states that it is a broad baseline and does not claim every reference applies to every product.

controls.reason: A register and its context fields are objective, but determining applicable jurisdictions, contracts, safety impacts, and sector requirements needs specialist judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: The applicability register records system type, users, data, jurisdictions, sector, contracts, safety impact, suppliers, and deployment model.

controls.reason: Issuing-body publication metadata is authoritative and can be queried and timestamped before each audit, procurement, certification, or compliance claim.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every standards claim references an issuing-body record showing the current published edition at a verification time preceding the claim.

controls.reason: Authoritative publication statuses can be mapped to an exact enumeration and compared with each crosswalk entry.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every referenced document's status matches the issuing body's current published, draft, committee-draft, proposed, guidance, or awareness classification.

controls.reason: Required conformance records can cite a licensed authoritative edition with an integrity digest rather than relying on reproduced corpus text.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every conformance assessment references an authorized authoritative text edition and verified digest.

controls.reason: Selecting all sector-specific standards for regulated domains requires current legal and domain expertise; the listed sectors are illustrative rather than complete.
Clause-to-control mappings are finite structured relationships with required owner, evidence, and exception references.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every applicable standards clause or outcome maps to local control identifiers, owners, evidence, and any exception identifiers.

controls.reason: A one-year interval and enumerated change events allow register review timestamps to be checked against a finite trigger ledger.

deterministic_clauses.statement: The standards register has an authenticated review no more than one year old.
Each recorded jurisdiction, product, data, incident, contract, or standards-revision event links to a later register review.

controls.reason: Outcome text can be required, but deciding whether it is explicit enough and faithfully represents user, business, regulatory, risk, or platform intent requires review.

deterministic_clauses.statement: The work item contains a nonempty outcome statement and declares its outcome source category.

controls.reason: Approval signatures and named sections are objective, but completeness and adequacy of scope, assumptions, constraints, dependencies, and criteria are contextual.

deterministic_clauses.statement: The work item records scope, non-scope, assumptions, constraints, dependencies, acceptance criteria, and authenticated approval.

controls.reason: Requirement-to-test links are objective, but whether functional and quality requirements are genuinely testable requires semantic judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every declared functional and quality requirement has a resolvable link to at least one test or verification method.

controls.reason: Relevance of user research and stakeholders and whether validation is complete are accountable product and research judgments.
Requirement categories can be checked, but deciding which privacy, security, accessibility, reliability, data, support, and lifecycle requirements are relevant and complete is contextual.

deterministic_clauses.statement: The work item has a requirement entry or explicit applicability decision for each named domain.

controls.reason: Satisfaction of requirements, justification of trade-offs, and absence of unnecessary complexity require architecture and product judgment.
Whether system, data, identity, trust, state, failure, operation, and migration implications are understood is a broad human-assurance claim without a fixed protocol.
Decision records are observable, but identifying every material decision and meaningful alternative requires architecture and risk judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every decision marked material links to a versioned record containing considered alternatives.

controls.reason: Completeness of threat, abuse, privacy, accessibility, and failure analysis requires multidisciplinary specialist review of an open-ended risk space.
Design artifacts for compatibility and lifecycle paths can be required, but adequacy for rollout, recovery, and retirement depends on change-specific context.

deterministic_clauses.statement: The work item links to versioned compatibility, rollout, rollback or roll-forward, and retirement design records.

controls.reason: Correctness, readability, cohesion, simplicity, and contextual conformance to standards are semantic code-review judgments that fixed syntax checks cannot settle.
Applying SOLID, DRY, KISS, YAGNI, reuse, and abstraction contextually is explicitly a design judgment and mechanical enforcement would be harmful.
Safe handling of all inputs, outputs, identities, authorization, errors, concurrency, resources, configuration, and secrets is an open-ended correctness and security claim.
Approval, support status, licenses, pins, inventory, and monitoring are checkable, but dependency necessity is an architecture and product judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every declared dependency has approval, support status, license, exact version pin, inventory entry, and active monitoring evidence.

controls.reason: Known code paths, flags, and privileges can be inventoried and lifecycle records checked, but proving no dead, debug, temporary, stale, or obsolete item remains is unbounded.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every item in the approved temporary-or-obsolete inventory is removed or has owner, rationale, and expiry lifecycle metadata.

controls.reason: Test-suite results are objective, but deciding which test levels are applicable and when testing is complete requires context and risk judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every test level declared applicable has a current completed result bound to the work item artifact.

controls.reason: Declared scenario coverage is measurable, but complete positive, negative, boundary, race, retry, failure, recovery, migration, and misuse scope is contextual.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every scenario in the approved coverage matrix links to a current test result.

controls.reason: The rule asks for evidence, so a finite objective registry can require a current bound evidence link for each named quality domain.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Each applicable security, privacy, accessibility, performance, reliability, compatibility, and data-quality objective has current evidence bound to the work item.

controls.reason: Mutation and skip checks are objective, but complete defect sensitivity and absence of hidden flakiness are empirical claims without a fixed confidence protocol.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Each test links to its claimed defect class, has a current sensitivity result, is not configured skipped, and reports observed retry or flake history.

controls.reason: Exact artifact digests and versioned representative configuration allow integrity comparison and bounded verification against the releasable pair.

deterministic_clauses.statement: The work item identifies the exact releasable artifact digest and production-representative configuration version.
Current verification results are bound to that exact artifact and configuration pair.

controls.reason: Required supply-chain artifacts have exact digests, signatures, attestations, and approval references whose availability and integrity are decidable.

deterministic_clauses.statement: The build provenance, artifact digest, SBOM, required signature or attestation, and required approvals are present and bound to the releasable artifact.

controls.reason: Configuration and delivery inputs are finite versioned records whose review approvals and deployment ordering can be checked exactly.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Configuration, migrations, feature flags, infrastructure, dependencies, and deployment order each have version identifiers and authenticated review records.

controls.reason: Readiness of monitoring, telemetry, SLOs, runbooks, capacity, and support is a broad operational acceptance decision, not mere artifact presence.
A finite release recovery plan can enumerate rollback, roll-forward, restoration, reconciliation, and incident scenarios with exact expected outcomes.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every applicable recovery and incident scenario in the release plan has a current successful bounded test result.

controls.reason: Human and supplier availability and communication readiness require accountable confirmation of qualifications, coverage, commitments, and release needs.
Document existence and timestamps are objective, but applicability, completeness, and whether content is current enough require domain review.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every documentation type declared applicable links to a version bound to the work item and not superseded before assessment.

controls.reason: Known limitation, risk, exception, and deferred-work registers can be required as explicit release-record collections.

deterministic_clauses.statement: The work item contains explicit linked registers for known limitations, residual risks, exceptions, and deferred work.

controls.reason: Prepared release, migration, deprecation, and support documents are finite versioned artifacts whose presence and bindings can be checked.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Each applicable release-note, migration, deprecation, and support-information artifact exists and is bound to the work item version.

controls.reason: Temporary-control ownership and expiry are exact required record fields.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every temporary control has exactly one accountable owner and a future expiry timestamp.

controls.reason: Change identifiers and immutable evidence or decision references make exact linkage and retention objectively decidable.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every retained evidence and decision record links to the exact change identifier and immutable version.

controls.reason: A finite blocker register and allowed terminal states can prove whether every blocker is resolved before acceptance.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every release blocker in the bound register has a resolved state or authenticated authorized exception before final acceptance.

controls.reason: Risk values and approval records are observable, but completeness of known residual risks and comparison with authorized tolerance require accountable risk judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every residual risk in the approved register has a value at or below its recorded authorized tolerance or a current authorized exception.

controls.reason: Required review roles and sign-offs are a finite approval matrix with identities, independence metadata, and signatures.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every review and sign-off required by the approval matrix has a valid authenticated completion record.

controls.reason: Declared failure scenarios can be tested, but proving sufficient detection, containment, disabling, recovery, and communication for all failures is unbounded and contextual.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every failure scenario in the approved release-risk inventory has evidence for detection, containment, disablement, recovery, and communication.

controls.reason: Post-deployment validation and observation criteria are explicit release-plan fields with fixed metrics, thresholds, and windows.

deterministic_clauses.statement: The release plan defines validation checks and observation metrics, thresholds, start times, and end times.

controls.reason: An approved critical-journey inventory and bound end-to-end result registry make missing successful evidence mechanically decidable.

deterministic_clauses.statement: The release record enumerates applicable critical user, operator, administrator, recovery, cancellation, and deletion journeys.
Every inventoried critical journey has current successful end-to-end evidence bound to the releasable artifact.

controls.reason: Requirement and objective fields and evidence links are checkable, but materiality and whether observed behavior truly contradicts intent require contextual review.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every requirement or quality objective marked material is defined and links to current verification evidence and observed results.

controls.reason: Applicable identity-control areas and required independent reviews form a finite matrix whose evidence and reviewer separation can be checked.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Each applicable authentication, authorization, privileged-access, recovery, and tenant-isolation area has current verification by a reviewer independent under the approved policy.

controls.reason: Exposure records, exploit status, mitigation tests, and exceptions are observable, but criticality and mitigation sufficiency require security and risk-owner judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every known exposure marked critical or actively exploited has current mitigation evidence or a current authenticated authorized exception.

controls.reason: For each recorded exposure, incident actions have exact item bindings and terminal states, allowing revocation, rotation, containment, and investigation completion to be checked.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every exposed secret, key, credential, token, personal record, or sensitive artifact has a unique incident item record.
Each incident item records completed revocation or invalidation, rotation where applicable, containment, and investigation before release approval.

controls.reason: Rehearsal, verification, and recovery evidence are observable, but destructive, irreversible, high-volume, and safely recovered are context-dependent data-risk judgments.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every data change marked destructive, irreversible, or high-volume has current rehearsal, post-change verification, and recovery evidence.

controls.reason: Approved restoration, disaster-recovery, rollback, and roll-forward objectives provide exact time, point, integrity, and continuity limits for exercises.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every applicable recovery path has a current successful exercise result meeting all approved objectives.

controls.reason: Test and model records can show what is known, but expected peak, burst, largest-tenant, abuse, and dependency-failure scenarios require forecasts and risk selection.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Each expected-behavior scenario in the approved capacity and abuse model has a documented expectation and current evidence.

controls.reason: Approved critical journeys and versioned quality objectives create a finite matrix whose current measurements can be compared with exact thresholds.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every critical journey maps to applicable availability, latency, correctness, durability, freshness, accessibility, security, privacy, and safety objectives.
Current bound evidence for every mapped objective satisfies its approved threshold.

controls.reason: Monitor tests are objective, but complete detection coverage for material corruption and control bypass depends on failure-model completeness and materiality judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every failure mode in the approved critical-journey, corruption, bypass, and telemetry-loss inventory has a current successful monitor-detection test.

controls.reason: Responder qualification, authorization, and actual availability during launch and early operation are human readiness facts requiring accountable confirmation.
Procedure existence is objective, but deciding which incident, communication, supplier, and breach procedures are required by risk needs specialist judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every procedure type declared required in the approved risk plan resolves to a current versioned document.

controls.reason: Determining mandatory obligations and whether they are met requires current legal, regulatory, contractual, accessibility, privacy, payment, safety, and procurement authority.
A signed provenance graph can deterministically trace the production digest through build inputs, reviewed source, dependencies, tests, and approvals.

deterministic_clauses.statement: The production artifact digest has an unbroken verified provenance chain to reviewed source, declared dependencies, trusted build identity, test results, and approval.

controls.reason: Support status and plan fields are observable, but criticality and adequacy of a compensating control or funded replacement plan require risk-owner judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every declared critical end-of-life component links to current compensating-control test evidence and a funded replacement plan with owner and date.

controls.reason: Proving that disclosure, corruption, duplicate charging, irreversible finance effects, or unsafe acts are no longer possible is an open-ended safety and correctness claim.
Declared recovery topology can expose single points and test alternatives, but undocumented human procedures and completeness of recovery paths make the full negative claim unbounded.

deterministic_clauses.statement: The approved recovery graph has no single recovery node contrary to objectives, and every declared alternative path has a current test result.

controls.reason: Artifact and configuration mismatches and timestamps are objective, but deciding whether an intervening untested change is material requires contextual impact analysis.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Evidence is rejected when its bound artifact or configuration differs from the release or when a later change marked material lacks reassessment.

controls.reason: Append-only status history and exception references can reveal blocker relabeling or suppression and verify that every waiver has authorized evidence-based acceptance.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every blocker status transition is preserved, and any suppression, waiver, or Not Applicable transition links to a valid authorized risk-acceptance record.

controls.reason: Concrete hold, stop, rollback, roll-forward, incident, and communication thresholds are exact required predeployment fields.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Before deployment, the release plan defines measurable thresholds and actions for hold, stop, rollback, roll-forward, incident, and communication.

controls.reason: Seriousness and whether an anomaly, test failure, mismatch, or security signal is adequately explained require accountable technical and risk judgment.
Determining the only true rationale for proceeding from deadline, revenue, sunk cost, pressure, or unsupported confidence requires interpreting human intent and decision context.
Manipulation, discrimination, accessibility, safety, unlawfulness, and lawful constraint require ethical, accessibility, safety, and legal authority.
Essential records, data integrity, and user rights across failure, migration, recovery, and retirement require legal, records, privacy, and architecture judgment over broad lifecycle scenarios.
The named accountability domains form a finite owner matrix whose identity references and exact-one cardinality can be validated.

deterministic_clauses.statement: The organization register identifies one accountable owner for product, service, data, security, privacy, operations, and residual risk.

controls.reason: The final package fields are exact immutable identifiers and version values whose presence and integrity references can be checked.

deterministic_clauses.statement: The final evidence package contains release identifier, source commits, tags, artifact digests, configuration versions, migration versions, and feature-flag states.

controls.reason: The required final scope, inventory, and diagram artifacts are a finite package manifest whose presence and version bindings are decidable.

deterministic_clauses.statement: The final evidence package contains final scope, asset inventory, architecture diagrams, deployment diagrams, and data-flow diagrams bound to the release.

controls.reason: The named data-governance artifacts are finite required package entries with exact versions and integrity references.

deterministic_clauses.statement: The final evidence package contains a data inventory, classification, retention schedule, and privacy records bound to the release context.

controls.reason: Threat, abuse, risk, and exception artifacts are explicit required package entries whose presence and release binding can be validated.

deterministic_clauses.statement: The final evidence package contains the threat model, abuse-case assessment, risk register, and accepted-exception register.

controls.reason: The package can require a versioned applicability register containing each named requirement domain and authoritative source reference.

deterministic_clauses.statement: The final evidence package contains applicable legal, privacy, accessibility, security, regulatory, and contractual requirements with source versions.

controls.reason: A traceability graph has resolvable relationships whose required coverage and referential integrity are mechanically decidable.

deterministic_clauses.statement: The final evidence package maps every requirement to tests and every control to evidence with valid identifiers.

controls.reason: Each named test-result class is a finite required package entry with artifact, configuration, and execution bindings.

deterministic_clauses.statement: The final evidence package contains current functional, integration, contract, system, regression, and user-acceptance results for all applicable test classes.

controls.reason: Browser, device, localization, usability, and accessibility result artifacts can be enumerated and checked against the declared applicability matrix.

deterministic_clauses.statement: The final evidence package contains release-bound results for each applicable browser, device, localization, usability, and accessibility test class.

controls.reason: Performance result types are explicit package entries whose existence and binding to declared conditions can be checked.

deterministic_clauses.statement: The final evidence package contains release-bound performance, load, stress, spike, endurance, and capacity results for every applicable type.

controls.reason: The resilience and recovery result classes form a finite manifest with exact release and scenario bindings.

deterministic_clauses.statement: The final evidence package contains resilience, dependency-failure, failover, rollback, roll-forward, and recovery results for every applicable class.

controls.reason: Security scan, review, threat-validation, and penetration-test results are explicit package artifacts with tool, scope, date, and release bindings.

deterministic_clauses.statement: The final evidence package contains current security-scan, code-review, threat-validation, and penetration-test results for each applicable class.

controls.reason: SBOM, license report, provenance, signatures, and attestations have exact digests and cryptographic or referential integrity checks.

deterministic_clauses.statement: The final evidence package contains a verified SBOM, license report, build provenance, artifact signatures, and attestation evidence bound to the artifact digest.

controls.reason: The six named review areas are explicit required package records with environment and configuration bindings.

deterministic_clauses.statement: The final evidence package contains current infrastructure, network, DNS, certificate, secrets, and production-configuration review records.

controls.reason: Backup, restoration, disaster-recovery, and continuity evidence are finite package entries whose scenario and execution bindings can be validated.

deterministic_clauses.statement: The final evidence package contains current backup, restoration, disaster-recovery, and continuity evidence for every applicable plan.

controls.reason: The named operational drill evidence classes are finite required package entries with dates, participants, and release-context references.

deterministic_clauses.statement: The final evidence package contains incident-response, on-call, alerting, runbook, and communications drill evidence.

controls.reason: Monitoring and telemetry review types are explicit package entries whose source and review bindings can be checked.

deterministic_clauses.statement: The final evidence package contains monitoring, dashboard, synthetic-check, logging, audit, and telemetry review records.

controls.reason: Third-party risk, contract, subprocessor, and continuity review records are finite package artifacts tied to the supplier inventory.

deterministic_clauses.statement: The final evidence package contains current third-party risk, contract, subprocessor, and continuity review records for every applicable supplier.

controls.reason: Open defect, risk, and exception registers are explicit package artifacts with immutable versions.

deterministic_clauses.statement: The final evidence package contains current open-defect, risk, and exception registers.

controls.reason: Exception identifiers can be joined to a fixed required field set, making omissions mechanically decidable.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every exception in the final package records owner, impact, compensating control, monitoring, remediation plan, and expiry.

controls.reason: Deployment, recovery-path, and post-deployment validation plans are explicit release-bound package artifacts.

deterministic_clauses.statement: The final evidence package contains deployment, rollback or roll-forward, and post-deployment validation plans bound to the release.

controls.reason: An approval matrix and signed decision record allow required approvals, sign-offs, and rationale presence to be checked exactly.

deterministic_clauses.statement: The final evidence package contains every required authenticated approval and sign-off plus the final decision rationale.

controls.reason: Maintainer identities and domain coverage are objective, but qualification across eleven disciplines requires accountable professional judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: The corpus roster names an owner and active maintainers covering product, engineering, UX, security, privacy, data, quality, delivery, operations, and legal domains.

controls.reason: The annual maximum interval and authoritative major-standards revision events allow exact review-deadline checks.

deterministic_clauses.statement: The corpus has an authenticated review no more than one year old.
Every recorded major revision of a tracked standard links to a later corpus review.

controls.reason: Incident and finding records can trigger reviews, but materiality, privacy harm, safety events, and near misses require contextual or specialist classification.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every qualifying event in the approved incident and finding ledger links to a later corpus review.

controls.reason: Entry events for jurisdictions, sectors, user populations, deployment models, and contractual regimes can be matched to later corpus review records.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every recorded entry into a new jurisdiction, sector, user population, deployment model, or contractual regime links to a later corpus review.

controls.reason: Feature-addition and review dates are observable, but sensitive and high-impact classification requires privacy, safety, and risk judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every qualifying capability addition in the approved change ledger links to a later corpus review.

controls.reason: Issuing-body registries provide authoritative status values that can be compared with every tracked standards record.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every tracked standard's published, amended, withdrawn, superseded, or draft status matches its issuing body's current record.

controls.reason: Baseline and draft statuses plus transition-decision records make unauthorized draft replacement mechanically detectable.

deterministic_clauses.statement: No current published baseline is replaced by a draft unless a prior authenticated transition decision explicitly authorizes early adoption.

controls.reason: Immutable corpus versions and release or audit references can prove historical preservation and exact-version binding.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every historical corpus version remains retrievable by digest, and every release or audit references exactly one such version.

controls.reason: Corpus diffs enumerate added, changed, moved, and retired controls, allowing exact changelog coverage and required fields.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every control change detected between corpus versions has a changelog entry with action, rationale, and owner.

controls.reason: Detecting silent weakening during consolidation requires semantic comparison of intent and assurance strength, not merely textual or structural diffing.
Source links and change records are objective, but deciding how incidents, research, threats, suppliers, and operations should refine controls requires maintainer judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every control change claiming an evidence basis links to the incident, defect, research, support, threat, supplier, or operational source record.

controls.reason: Duplicate meaning, overlap, and standalone usability are semantic editorial judgments that syntax and similarity scores cannot decide reliably.
Markdown links, headings, checklist tokens, front matter, encoding, and relative paths have exact parsers and bounded repository targets.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every corpus Markdown file passes the versioned link, heading, checklist-syntax, front-matter, encoding, and relative-path validators.

controls.reason: Required category-file sections are exact structural headings or front-matter fields that can be parsed from the bounded corpus.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every category file contains purpose, applicability, universal controls, evidence expectations, and interpretation-boundary sections.

controls.reason: Bounded detectors can find known secret and sensitive-data patterns, but proving absence of all personal, internal, or proprietary information is unbounded.

deterministic_clauses.statement: All publication files have current results from approved secret, personal-data, internal-URL, and proprietary-information detectors.

controls.reason: Technology neutrality and the relevance of framework, vendor, language, and platform references require semantic editorial judgment.
Whether a control is genuinely technology-specific and a module is clearly conditional are semantic classification and information-architecture judgments.
With versioned metric definitions, corpus assessments and operational registers supply bounded counts and rates for each named measure.

deterministic_clauses.statement: The corpus program records defined measurements for use, ambiguity, Not Applicable patterns, exception recurrence, and escaped defects.

controls.reason: Confirming that a risk or requirement no longer exists before retiring a control requires accountable domain, legal, and risk judgment.
Release-note and migration-guide presence is objective, but classifying corpus changes as material requires editorial and user-impact judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every corpus change marked material has versioned release notes and a migration guide.

controls.reason: The production-service inventory is finite, so named business and engineering owner fields can be checked for every service.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every production service has one active business owner and one active engineering owner.

controls.reason: Declared integration and operational-asset inventories are finite and support exact owner-cardinality checks.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every third-party integration, dashboard, alert, runbook, scheduled job, and background process in the approved inventories has an active owner.

controls.reason: Primary, backup, and identity status records are objective, but whether ownership remains valid under every leave or personnel scenario includes qualification and coverage judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every owned asset has active primary and backup owner coverage with no gap during recorded leave, holiday, or personnel-change intervals.

controls.reason: The escalation contact categories are an exact required field set with resolvable identity or provider references.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every escalation path contains primary, secondary, management, security, privacy or legal, and provider contacts.

controls.reason: Identity and access event times can be compared, but promptly has no maximum delay and appropriate role-change access requires entitlement judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every recorded offboarding or role-change event links to resulting access removals or adjustments with timestamps.

controls.reason: Periodically supplies no review interval, event trigger, or freshness threshold, so identical ownership-review dates can receive different outcomes.
Impact classification across confidentiality, finance, safety, regulation, reputation, and trust is an accountable multidisciplinary risk judgment.
Threat-source categories can be required in a model, but identifying complete relevant actors and failure sources requires contextual threat analysis.

deterministic_clauses.statement: The threat model addresses external attackers, abusive users, insiders, compromised accounts, bots, automated agents, social engineering, and accidental failures with entries or explicit applicability decisions.

controls.reason: Foreseeable misuse and abuse are open-ended adversarial and human-behavior scenarios that require threat, safety, and product judgment.
Risk identifiers form a finite register whose owner, likelihood, impact, treatment, evidence, and review-date fields can be checked exactly.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every risk in the approved register has owner, likelihood, impact, treatment, evidence reference, and review date.

controls.reason: Accepted residual risks and accepting identities are explicit signed register fields with authorization references.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every accepted residual risk records its value, authenticated accepting people, and their authorization references.

controls.reason: Whether launch scope remains within risk appetite requires accountable interpretation of aggregate and interacting risks, not only field comparison.
Exception timestamps and compensating-control test records make automatic expiry and test completion directly decidable.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every exception expires automatically at its recorded expiry time.
Every active exception's compensating controls have current successful test evidence.

controls.reason: Mapping records are objective, but whether a verification standard is recognized and the mapping is substantively faithful requires security-governance judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every security control links to a clause or outcome in the organization's approved verification-standard registry.

controls.reason: Selecting applicable legal and organizational privacy requirements and validating substantive control mappings requires privacy and legal authority.
Once the conformance target is selected, its control or criterion identifiers can be mapped exactly to accessibility controls.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every accessibility control links to one or more criteria in the versioned selected conformance target.

controls.reason: Identifying and resolving conflicts across product, law, security, privacy, accessibility, and technology is an accountable multidisciplinary trade-off decision.
Resolution, trade-off, and approval records are explicit governance artifacts whose presence, identity, and signatures are mechanically decidable.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every registered requirements conflict links to a documented resolution, stated trade-offs, and required authenticated approvals.
